questions.question: What is the meaning of National income?
questions.solution:
National Income is the total value of all final goods and services produced by the country in certain year.

National Income = C + I + G + (X - M)

Where, C stands for Total Consumption Expenditure

I = Total Investment Expenditure

G = Total Government Expenditure

X - M = Export - Import

questions.question: In economic terms, national development is __________.
questions.solution: National development is the ability of a county or countries to improve the social welfare of the people e.g. by providing social amenities like quality education, potable water, transportation infrastructure, medical care, etc.

questions.question: Which right allows citizens to move to the court if they believe that any of their fundamental rights have been violated by the state?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is option __**4**__, i.e. __**Right to Constitution Remedies**__.

__
 
• When any of our rights are violated we can seek a remedy through courts. If it is a Fundamental Right we can directly approach the Supreme Court or the High Court of a state.
 
• Article 32 of the Indian Constitution has been described as the ‘heart and soul’ of the Indian Constitution by Dr. B. R. Ambedkar.
 
• It gives a citizen the right to approach the Supreme Court to get resorted any of the fundamental rights in case of their violation.
 
• It is also known as; Right to Constitutional Remedies__.

questions.question: Which part of the Indian Constitution has often been referred to as its ‘conscience’?
questions.solution:
Option **2** is correct, i.e. __**Fundamental Rights**__.

__
 
• The section on **Fundamental Rights**__ has often been referred to as the ‘**conscience**’ of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Fundamental Rights, protect citizens against the arbitrary and absolute exercise of power by the State.
 
• The Constitution, thus, guarantees the rights of individuals against the State as well as against other individuals.

**Extra information:**

 
• Under Part-III (article 12 - 35) of the constitution every citizen has provided 6 fundamental rights.
 
• A total of seven rights were originally provided by the Constitution.
 
• 44th amendment (1978 A.D.) removed the right to property and made a legal right (300A).
 
• The fundamental rights secure the natural rights of all citizens and it was taken from the constitution of the U.S.A.

questions.solution: The Third Battle of Panipat fought on January 14, 1761 between the Marathas and forces of the Afghan ruler Ahmad Shah Abdali and his allies was one of the biggest and most significant battles of the 18th century in India. The Marathas were defeated in that war.

questions.question: Summer solstice in Northern Hemisphere occurs on which date of the year?
questions.solution: The summer solstice occurs on June 21 in the Northern Hemisphere and occur 22 December each year in the Southern Hemisphere. The same dates in the opposite hemisphere are referred to as the winter solstice.

questions.question: Eurasia is the combined landmass of Asia and ______.
questions.solution: Eurasia is a combined continental landmass of Europe and Asia.

questions.question: When the right ventricle of heart contracts, the blood goes to ______.
questions.solution: From right ventricle, the deoxygenated blood goes through pulmonary arteries to lungs for oxygenation.

questions.question: A digestive enzyme, salivary amylase, in the saliva begins digestion of which of the following?
questions.solution: Salivary glands in your mouth make salivary amylase, which begins the digestive process by breaking down starch when you chew your food, converting it into maltose, a smaller carbohydrate.

questions.question: In 28 - day human ovarian cycle, ovulation occurs on ______.

questions.question: An ionic bond is formed by ______.
questions.solution: Ionic bond, also called the electrovalent bond, type of linkage formed from the electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions in a chemical compound. Such a bond forms when the valence (outermost) electrons of one atom are transferred permanently to another atom. The atom that loses the electrons becomes a positively charged ion (cation), while the one that gains them becomes a negatively charged ion (anion). questions.question: Acid rain that corrodes the marble of the Taj Mahal is made up of which acids?
questions.solution: Acid rain, or acid deposition, is a broad term that includes any form of precipitation with acidic components, such as sulphuric or nitric acid that fall to the ground from the atmosphere in wet or dry forms.

questions.question: Who invented Airplane?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Wright Brothers.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Wright Brothers:**

 
 
• Orville and Wilbur Wright (The Wright Brothers) invented the first aeroplane in 1903. 
 
• In order to make a biplane roll to the right or left, Wilbur came up with a straightforward solution in 1899.
 
• They used a kite to test the system before moving on to many gliders.
 
• The Wrights' first two gliders, which were flown in 1900 and 1901, didn't perform as well as they'd intended.
 
• The gliders were difficult to fully control and did not offer an adequate lift.
 
• In order to find the ideal wing form for an aeroplane, Wilbur and Orville constructed a wind tunnel and ran tests over the winter of 1901-1902.
 
• The Wrights developed a gasoline engine that was both light and strong enough to power an aeroplane during the winter of 1902-03 with the assistance of their mechanic, Charlie Taylor.
 
• They also developed a brand-new, powered aircraft and created the first real aeroplane propellers.
 
• The first prolonged, controlled flights in a powered aircraft were accomplished by Wilbur and Orville Wright on December 17, 1903.
 
• They took four flights on that day.
 
• The first Wright Flyer flight was made by Orville.
 
• The day's fourth trip was flown by Wilbur.
 
• The first practicable aeroplane in history was the 1905 Wright Flyer.

questions.question: Which of the following pair is INCORRECT with respect to Kumbh Mela?
questions.solution: Kumbh Mela or KumbhaMela is a mass Hindu pilgrimage of faith in which Hindus gather to bathe in a sacred or holy river. The main festival site is located on the banks of a river: the Ganges (Ganga) at Haridwar; the confluence (Sangam) of the Ganges and the Yamuna and the invisible Sarasvati at Allahabad; the Godavari at Nasik; and the Shipra at Ujjain.

questions.question: Who won the 2016 Arjuna Award for Boxing?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shiva Thapa.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Shiva Thapa **won the 2016 Arjuna Award for Boxing.
 
• He became the first Indian boxer to qualify for the 2016 Rio Olympics by entering the Asian Qualifying Tournament's final.
 
• Shiva Thapa participated in the 2012 London Olympics, and was the youngest Indian boxer to qualify for the Olympics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

About Arjun Award - 

 
• It was started in 1961 by the government of India. 
 
• Ministry of Youth Affairs and sports awards best sportspersons. 
 
• Those who have shown constantly good performance for 4 years at the international level will be chosen for this award. 
 
• The cash prize for the Arjuna Award is** ₹15 lakh**. The award also includes a bronze statuette of Arjuna, a certificate, and a ceremonial dress. 
 
• Krishna Das was the first person to be awarded the Arjun Award in 1984

questions.question: Other than India and Afghanistan which is the third participant country in Chabahar Trilateral agreement on transport and transit corridors?
questions.solution:
***The correct answer is Iran.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Chabahar Trilateral Agreement involves three key participants: India, Afghanistan, and Iran.
 
• This agreement aims to establish a transport and transit corridor through the Chabahar Port in Iran, providing a strategic route for trade and connectivity between these countries and beyond.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pakistan:** Pakistan is not part of the Chabahar Trilateral Agreement. In fact, Pakistan has its strategic port, Gwadar, which it is developing in collaboration with China as part of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC).
 
• **Kazakhstan: **Kazakhstan is not involved in the Chabahar Trilateral Agreement. While Kazakhstan is a Central Asian country with significant trade interests, it does not directly participate in this particular agreement focused on the Chabahar Port in Iran.
 
• **Bangladesh:** Bangladesh is not part of the Chabahar Trilateral Agreement. While Bangladesh is involved in various regional and international trade initiatives, it is not included in the specific agreement regarding the Chabahar Port.
